headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: CrewAI can write/execute locally while Perplexity ingests web content and may feed unverified outputs back into agent workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host filesystem and parse tool outputs in a shared-memory crew, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction stream. Perplexity runs vendor-hosted browsing/search and can surface raw web content. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, making injection plausible in default workflows, though not proven to be a shared channel.
conditions: IF CrewAI agents ingest Perplexity-generated text as instructions without provenance tags, injection is possible.
IF Perplexity returns web content that CrewAI later parses as prompts, the pathway activates.
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff format.
Require provenance labels on all Perplexity outputs before CrewAI consumes them.
Disable automatic tool execution on text received from Perplexity.
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like strings before deployment.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Perplexity processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context. If they share a workspace or the crew forwards sensitive files into Perplexity, data can leave the local environment to vendor-hosted inference. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is a plausible default-path leakage rather than certain exfiltration.
conditions: IF CrewAI passes secrets or crew data into Perplexity queries, those data leave the host boundary.
IF uploaded documents in Perplexity contain sensitive material originating from CrewAI, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Block secrets from being included in Perplexity prompts.
Use a redaction step before any CrewAI-to-Perplexity transfer.
Restrict Perplexity uploads to non-sensitive documents only.
Audit one end-to-end query for unintended sensitive fields.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has host filesystem write and shell execution, while Perplexity has no host write or shell capability. Their write surfaces do not overlap directly, so destructive contention is limited. The main conflict risk is only if an external orchestrator maps both onto the same mutable workspace, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator mounts the same writable directory into both agents, file contention becomes possible.
IF CrewAI is configured to modify files that Perplexity also reads from a shared workspace, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Separate working directories for the two agents.
Mount Perplexity inputs read-only where possible.
Avoid concurrent writes to any shared folder.
Check the orchestrator for implicit workspace sharing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate outputs from tools and browser results, and Perplexity’s Pro Search is designed to produce cited answers from browsing. If CrewAI treats Perplexity answers as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary, so the default risk is moderate rather than low.
conditions: IF CrewAI consumes Perplexity answers without independent verification, falsehoods can propagate.
IF CrewAI uses Perplexity output to trigger tools or write files, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before CrewAI acts on Perplexity output.
Require source links for any factual claim before use.
Limit Perplexity output to suggestions, not commands.
Sample-check one workflow for unverified handoff behavior.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI is open-source and host-run, while Perplexity is closed-source and vendor-hosted with browsing context and uploaded documents. Sensitive data handled by CrewAI can therefore flow into a third-party service with different retention and residency terms. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF CrewAI data includes regulated or contractual-sensitive content and is sent to Perplexity, compliance review is required.
IF Perplexity retention differs from the source data policy, a policy mismatch exists.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to Perplexity.
Use Perplexity only for non-regulated content.
Review vendor retention and residency terms.
Keep an audit log of all cross-agent transfers.
